findings: RISK (concrete, engineering): ADR 0001 carries a stale self-declared state that directly contradicts the repository's actual approval and implementation state, so any agent or gate that reads it as current-state evidence will make a wrong material decision. The ADR still asserts `Status: proposed` (docs/adr/0001-multi-agent-control-plane-boundary.md:3), marks all seven decisions HUMAN_PENDING (lines 149, 159, 169, 179, 189, 199, 235), gates Phase 1 on criteria 1-3 being HUMAN_PENDING with the rule 'Phase 1 may begin only when all of the following hold' (lines 273-283), and closes with 'No Phase-1 implementation has begun' (line 325). In the same repo, README.md records all seven decisions as HUMAN_APPROVED (README.md:118-124), calls the ADR 'accepted foundation' (README.md:89), and Phase-1..Phase-5 deliverables plus a live control plane exist and cite the ADR as binding (orchestrator/contract.md:6; docs/phase-2/0001-requirements-traceability.md:29 'ADR 0001 accepted; HUMAN_APPROVED decisions D1-D7').

The contradiction has already propagated: downstream documents disagree about the same authority object. Some treat the Decision 4/7 composition exception as still unapproved and blocking (docs/phase-5/security/g10/final/0001-g10-final-mitigation-analysis.md:81; docs/phase-5/final/0005-final-security-gate-evidence.md:39), while others record the same exception as executed ('O5 applied (raw-write actor set {zeko, cto})', docs/phase-5/security/g10/o3/0001-o3-implementation-package.md:6). Practical failure modes: an orchestrator honoring the ADR's entry-criteria gate blocks or re-opens work that is already approved and shipped; an orchestrator honoring the later docs proceeds on an exception whose approval is not traceable to the ADR that defines the exception process. Under AGENTS.md section 4 a SUPERSEDED/STALE context MUST NOT support material decisions, yet ADR 0001 contains no supersession, addendum, or status-transition marker to tell a reader it is stale.

MITIGATION (one, concrete): give ADR 0001 an explicit status/authority addendum and make the drift machine-detectable. (a) Append a 'Revision 3 - Status transition' block that sets Status: accepted, records the transition date and the authority source (pointer to README.md section 'Human decisions' rows 1-7, or to the dated audit/delegation record if one exists), restates each decision's current approval state, marks Phase-1 Entry Criteria 1-4 as satisfied/deferred with evidence pointers, and corrects the footer claim that no Phase-1 work has begun; keep the original decision text immutable so the record stays auditable. (b) Add one invariant to the existing tests/validate-config.py: parse the ADR's per-decision approval markers and the README approval table and fail the test when they disagree (and fail when the ADR status is 'proposed' while any phase-1+ deliverable is present). This converts a human-maintenance burden (already named as the Decision 6 risk, line 234) into a CI-enforced check, so future approval-state drift is caught before it reaches a gate.

structured.recommendation: Treat this as a documentation-authority reconciliation, not a redesign: ADR 0001's enforcement-layer decisions remain sound and are already implemented, but its status block is stale and is actively producing contradictory citations downstream. Action for the orchestrator: (1) have a Human confirm the authoritative approval record for decisions 1-7 and for the Decision 4/7 composition exception, with dates; (2) then author ADR 0001 Revision 3 as a status/authority addendum (Status: accepted, per-decision approval states, entry-criteria outcomes, corrected footer) without rewriting the original decision text, and add a supersession pointer so phase-5 docs citing 'HUMAN_PENDING' are corrected in the same pass; (3) extend tests/validate-config.py with a single ADR-vs-README approval-consistency invariant so this class of drift fails CI rather than reaching a gate. Do not widen the ADR's scope or reopen any decision as part of the fix - the defect is the record's staleness, not the decision content.
